note: Grouped by category for navigation as the roster grows. Keep new entries filed under an existing category from npc.schema.json's enum, in the matching block below, rather than appended at the end unsorted.

characters.name: Cole Calloway
characters.role: Patriarch of the Calloway Spread
personality: not cruel by his own lights
characters.hook: Birdie's father. He arranged her marriage to settle a water dispute and cannot understand why that isn't obviously the right call. A future reconciliation or rivalry beat for Birdie's arc runs through him.
voice_lines: A Calloway doesn't walk off a deal because she didn't like the terms.
You'll come back when the romance of it wears off.
I built this place so my children wouldn't have to gamble the way I did.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man in his fifties, weathered and upright, dressed better than his hands but not showy about it.
characters.art_prompt: Silver-haired rancher in a clean but worn canvas coat, string tie, standing very straight on his own porch. Confident posture, not a villain's sneer -- he believes he is right.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Referenced by fina_reyes and birdie_calloway's encounter hooks in characters.json.

characters.name: Hattie Calloway
characters.role: Birdie's mother
characters.hook: Wants Birdie back but won't cross Cole to say so directly. A softer entry point into the Calloway rivalry than Cole himself.
voice_lines: He isn't wrong often. That doesn't mean he's right about this.
Tell her the garden misses her. She'll know what I mean.
I raised her to have a spine. I don't know why I'm surprised she used it.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman in her late forties, practical dress, tired kindness in her face.
characters.art_prompt: A ranch matriarch on a porch step, apron over a plain dress, looking toward the horizon rather than at the viewer. Warm late light, quieter composition than Cole's.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Whit Calloway
characters.role: Birdie's older brother, heir to the Spread
characters.hook: Stands to inherit everything Birdie walked away from and cannot decide if he envies her or is furious at her. A rival or reluctant ally depending on later choices.
voice_lines: Funny how the one who left is the one everybody still asks about.
I didn't get a say either. I just didn't have anywhere else to go.
Tell her the fence line held. She'll know that took some doing.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-twenties, built for ranch work, dresses like his father wants him to.
characters.art_prompt: A young rancher on horseback checking a fence line, hat low, expression unreadable rather than openly hostile.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Tomas Reyes
characters.role: Fina's father, a respected vaquero at a neighboring outfit
personality: proud of Fina without saying so directly
characters.hook: Fina's continuity anchor and a source of vaquero-tradition rumors or a future encounter about her past.
voice_lines: She rides like her mother and argues like me. God help whoever marries her.
I taught her the rope. The temper she came with on her own.
A horse doesn't lie about who broke it right. Watch hers move.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late fifties, deeply sun-weathered, immaculate in his gear if nothing else.
characters.art_prompt: An older vaquero checking a saddle cinch, silver in his hair, worn but beautifully maintained tack -- read as expertise through the equipment's condition.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Sallie Voss
characters.role: Nettie Voss's daughter, learning the trading-post trade
characters.hook: Gives Nettie Voss a family tie and a future succession question -- does the trading post stay Nettie's sharp operation or does Sallie's warmer instinct change it. Not a recruitable companion; a town-continuity character.
voice_lines: Mother says I give too much credit. I say she gives none. We're both a little right.
I'll run this counter myself someday. I'm not in a hurry to prove when.
You want the fair price or the kind one? I can only promise one of those today.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, nineteen, dressed like her mother but softer about it, quick to smile.
characters.art_prompt: A young woman restocking shelves behind a trading-post counter, glancing toward an older shopkeeper (Nettie) with a mix of fondness and exasperation.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Jed Aldrich
characters.role: Foreman of the Calloway Spread's hands, reports directly to Cole
personality: loyal to Cole specifically, not the family generally
hard but fair with the hands he manages
privately sympathetic to Birdie without ever saying so to Cole
characters.hook: Gives the Calloway Spread a working-level voice distinct from the family itself -- someone who actually runs day-to-day operations and has his own read on the family drama.
voice_lines: Mr. Calloway doesn't need my opinion on his daughter. I keep it to myself and keep the hands working.
Whit's a fair boss in training. He'll be a better one once his father stops looking over his shoulder.
I've said my goodbyes to Birdie plenty of times when nobody was watching. Don't tell Cole that either.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late forties, weathered foreman's bearing, clearly the one who actually runs the daily work.
characters.art_prompt: A ranch foreman directing hands from horseback, competent and unhurried, watching the whole operation rather than any one task.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to the Calloway family records.

characters.name: Boyd Farrow
characters.role: A Calloway Spread ranch hand who's sweet on Sallie Voss
characters.hook: A small, human-scale thread connecting the Calloway Spread and Fort Griffin's Voss family -- a courtship subplot that doesn't need to involve the player's own companions at all.
voice_lines: I ride to Griffin more than the job strictly requires. Nobody's fooled, least of all Sallie.
Whit says I should just say something. Whit has never once said something either.
Her mother charges me full price at the counter. I think that means she approves.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-twenties, ordinary ranch hand, visibly nervous whenever a certain trading post comes up in conversation.
characters.art_prompt: A young ranch hand loitering with visible awkwardness near a trading-post counter, clearly working up the nerve to say something.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties Calloway Spread and sallie_voss together independent of the player.

characters.name: Dr. Adaeze Okafor
characters.role: Vashti Okafor's aunt, a respected physician in a larger town east of the county
personality: quietly proud of her niece's different path
occasionally writes offering Vashti a 'real' profession
characters.hook: Gives Vashti Okafor a family tie and a recurring gentle tension: an accomplished relative who thinks trapping and tracking is beneath what Vashti could achieve, without either being wrong.
voice_lines: I offered her a place training under me. She'd rather read tracks than pulses. We've made our peace with the difference.
She writes more than she lets on. I keep every letter.
Being a physician and being wrong sometimes are not exclusive facts. I remind young doctors of both.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, early fifties, composed and professional bearing, a physician's practiced calm.
characters.art_prompt: A physician at a proper city office desk, framed credentials visible, composed and dignified.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to vashti_okafor.

characters.name: Emmett Cross
characters.role: The Calloway family's lawyer, handling the water dispute referenced in Cole Calloway's record
personality: loyal to the family retainer, not necessarily to Cole personally
privately thinks the Birdie marriage arrangement was a mistake
characters.hook: Gives the arranged-marriage water dispute mentioned in cole_calloway's hook an actual person handling the paperwork, and a subtle crack of disagreement inside the Calloway camp.
voice_lines: I drew up the agreement. I didn't say it was wise. Those are different jobs.
Cole pays well and argues badly. I've learned to let the second part go.
If Birdie ever wants to contest the old arrangement formally, she has grounds. Nobody's asked me that yet.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-forties, precise formal dress, careful measured speech implied by posture alone.
characters.art_prompt: A lawyer at a cluttered desk of contracts and deeds, spectacles, deliberately neutral expression.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to cole_calloway and birdie_calloway's original arranged-marriage hook.

characters.name: Adaeze Okoye
characters.role: Louisa Okoye's younger sister, still waiting at their original destination town
personality: writes letters that arrive later than she'd like
characters.hook: Gives Louisa Okoye an ongoing reason to eventually resolve her situation -- a sister waiting, and letters that take too long to arrive, giving her arc a clock without forcing an ending.
voice_lines: The post takes so long. I don't know if my last three letters even reached her.
She always did the harder thing when the easier one was available. I don't know why I'm surprised.
Tell her the position's still open if she ever gets here. Tell her I miss her more than the position matters.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, mid-twenties, plain traveling-appropriate dress, worried but composed expression.
characters.art_prompt: A young woman writing a letter at a small desk in a modest room, worry visible in her posture despite steady handwriting.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to louisa_okoye.

characters.name: Tobias Ochoa
characters.role: Elena Ochoa's young son, referenced in her record without needing his own full entry until now
characters.hook: Gives Elena Ochoa's referenced son an actual (careful, non-romantic, age-appropriate) presence, matching the same deliberate-non-sexualization pattern already established for Tam.
voice_lines: Mama says Papa's not coming back. She doesn't say why. I've stopped asking, mostly.
I can already do more chores than she gives me credit for.
Are you going to stay, or are you like the others who just fix one thing and ride on?
characters.appearance_brief: A young boy in patched practical clothes, watchful and quiet, older in manner than in years.
characters.art_prompt: A boy standing in a homestead doorway watching visitors approach, arms crossed in imitation of an adult's wariness. Keep clearly childlike and non-sexualized, a background family character, not cast material -- same treatment as little_tam.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to elena_ochoa. Explicitly not romance-eligible; do not add to characters.json under any circumstance, matching little_tam's precedent exactly.

characters.name: Marta Teague
characters.role: Hollis Teague's mother and Orin Teague's wife, caught in the middle of the forge rivalry
personality: privately embarrassed by her husband's grudge
protective of her son's future in the trade
characters.hook: Gives Orin Teague's antagonist record a family context and a sympathetic pressure point -- someone who'd rather the rivalry with Naomi Freeman just end.
voice_lines: Orin's pride is going to cost Hollis his best years learning from someone worse than he could.
I've told my husband to let it go. I've told him twice this month.
If Hollis wants to learn from Naomi Freeman someday, I won't be the one who stops him.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, early forties, practical dress, tired but warm expression.
characters.art_prompt: A woman at a modest kitchen table, mending clothes, glancing toward a window facing the direction of her husband's forge.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to orin_teague and hollis_teague.

characters.name: Granny Combs
characters.role: Loretta Combs's grandmother, who taught her to quilt and started the county-memory tradition
personality: the actual origin of Loretta's project
carries the oldest stories in the county
characters.hook: Gives Loretta Combs's quilt-memory project a real origin and a source of the county's oldest, least-recorded history.
voice_lines: I started stitching what I saw so it wouldn't just disappear when I did. Loretta just does it better than I ever did.
Ask me about the county forty years back. Ask me before you can't anymore.
My hands don't hold a needle steady these days. Hers do. That's how it should work.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, mid-seventies, frail but alert, surrounded by fabric and the visible evidence of a lifetime's work.
characters.art_prompt: An elderly woman in a rocking chair surrounded by quilting fragments and old fabric scraps, sharp attentive eyes despite her age.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to loretta_combs and is a plausible source of additional county lore/rumors for a future writer to draw on.

characters.name: Reed Hargrove
characters.role: Owner of the Hargrove outfit, a newer and scrappier rival than the Calloway Spread
personality: genuinely believes he's owed the shortcut he's about to take
characters.hook: A second, distinct rival outfit so every competitive beat doesn't run through the Calloways. Where the Calloway Spread is established and tidy, the Hargrove outfit is new money, overleveraged, and willing to cut a corner Cole Calloway wouldn't.
voice_lines: Water rights go to whoever gets there first with a deed and a lawyer. I've got both.
The Calloways had thirty years' head start. I don't have thirty years.
Call it aggressive. I call it not waiting to be someone else's story.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, early thirties, expensive gear worn a little too new, restless energy.
characters.art_prompt: A young rancher in barely-broken-in boots and a too-clean hat, standing over a survey map spread on a wagon tailgate, impatient posture.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Cass Hargrove
characters.role: Reed's sister and equal partner in the Hargrove outfit
personality: the actual brains of the operation
underestimated on purpose and uses it
characters.hook: Runs the numbers Reed's ambition writes checks against. A more interesting rival conversation than Reed alone -- she'll deal fairly if the deal is actually good for her outfit.
voice_lines: My brother sells the vision. I collect on it. Talk to me if you want the real terms.
Let him have the big talk. I'll have the water rights.
I don't need you to like us. I need the count to add up.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, late twenties, sharply practical dress, always has a ledger within reach.
characters.art_prompt: A rancher-businesswoman reviewing a ledger against a tally of cattle at a corral fence, unimpressed expression, competent posture.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Milo Pratt
characters.role: A Hargrove hand who doesn't love where the outfit is heading
personality: quietly looking for a way out
characters.hook: A sympathetic crack in the rival outfit -- a possible source of information or even a future recruit if the Hargrove rivalry sours enough that he'd rather ride for someone else.
voice_lines: I signed on to punch cattle, not to run another outfit off good water.
Don't tell Reed I said that. Don't tell Cass either, she'd just agree and do it anyway.
There's outfits I'd rather ride for. I just haven't said so out loud yet.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-twenties, ordinary trail hand, nothing about him stands out on purpose.
characters.art_prompt: An unremarkable trail hand coiling rope by a chuck wagon, glancing toward his own outfit's boss with visible discomfort.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Suze Kirwan
characters.role: Foreman of the Hargrove outfit's hands, more competent than her employers deserve
personality: loyal to the paycheck more than the family
characters.hook: A working-level counterpart to Jed Aldrich on the Hargrove side -- the actual reason the newer, scrappier outfit functions at all despite Reed's overreach.
voice_lines: Reed has ideas. I have the actual job of making them not fall apart.
Cass at least does her own math. I respect that more than I respect Reed's confidence.
I'll work for whoever pays on time. Today that's the Hargroves. Ask me again next season.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, mid-thirties, no-nonsense trail gear, clearly the most competent person on the Hargrove payroll.
characters.art_prompt: A ranch foreman checking tack and gear with visible competence, unimpressed expression aimed just off-camera at her employer.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to reed_hargrove and cass_hargrove.

characters.name: Pardo
characters.role: The outfit's own senior hand, present since before the room's story starts
personality: the one who actually taught the player the ropes years back
characters.hook: Background texture for the player's own outfit, distinct from the recruited companions -- someone who was already there, not someone being courted. A source of grounded, unromantic trail wisdom.
voice_lines: Herd doesn't care whose idea this trip was. Feed it, water it, count it.
I've buried two bosses. Try not to make it three.
You ask a lot of questions for a man who already knows the answer.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-forties, permanently sun-cured, moves like every motion is considered.
characters.art_prompt: A senior trail hand checking a horse's hoof, unhurried, weathered leather gear that's clearly decades old and well kept.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Distinct from any recruited companion -- he does not leave the outfit or get a relationship arc.

characters.name: "Young" Dutch
characters.role: The outfit's newest and youngest hand
characters.hook: A counterweight to Pardo: the outfit's future rather than its past. Useful for a scene that needs someone to ask the obvious question everyone else stopped asking.
voice_lines: Is it always this much walking? Nobody told me it was this much walking.
Pardo says I'll stop asking questions in about ten years. I don't believe him.
First outfit that's ever paid me on time. I'd walk to Griffin twice for that.
characters.appearance_brief: A young adult man, gear too new, still figuring out how to wear a hat properly.
characters.art_prompt: A young trail hand fumbling with a coil of rope, eager expression, gear noticeably less worn than everyone around him.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Cutter Boyle
characters.role: A hired gun working the edges of the county for whoever pays
personality: has walked away from jobs before
characters.hook: A mercenary antagonist distinct from Silas's desperation -- Boyle isn't cornered, he's a professional, which makes him negotiable in a way a cornered man isn't. Useful if a later encounter needs an antagonist who can be talked out of a job rather than only fought.
voice_lines: I don't get paid enough to hate you personally. Take that as comfort or don't.
Somebody's always willing to pay more. Ask them first before you ask me to stop.
I've walked off three jobs this year. This one's not decided yet.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, forty, plain trail gear built for function, no flash on the gun rig.
characters.art_prompt: A hired gun leaning against a fence post, arms crossed, watching from a distance rather than confronting directly. Understated, not a mustache-twirling design.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: The Widow Stroud
characters.role: A moneylender operating out of Fort Griffin with an interest in outfits that fall behind
characters.hook: A non-violent antagonist: financial pressure rather than a gun. If the outfit ever needs money fast, she's who lends it, and she never needs to threaten anyone -- the terms do that on their own.
voice_lines: I don't want your herd. I want what your herd is worth, on the date we agreed.
Interest doesn't care whether your trip was hard. Neither, regrettably, do I.
I've never once raised my voice collecting a debt. I've rarely needed to twice.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, early fifties, dressed well but not ostentatiously, composed in a way that reads as controlled rather than warm.
characters.art_prompt: A well-dressed widow at a writing desk with an open ledger and a coffee going cold, calm and unhurried posture, the numbers doing the intimidating rather than her expression.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Alma Okafor
characters.role: The outfit's point rider, reads the trail ahead before the herd commits to it
personality: trusted by Pardo, which is not easily earned
characters.hook: A third piece of the outfit's own background crew, distinct from Pardo (institutional memory) and Dutch (green enthusiasm) -- she's the one whose judgment the trail actually depends on day to day.
voice_lines: Ground's soft past that ridge. Take the herd around, not through.
I ride ahead so nobody's surprised. Surprised is how outfits lose stock.
Pardo trusts my eyes. That took two years. Yours is still open for negotiation.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, thirty, lean and alert, dressed for long hours in the saddle rather than for looks.
characters.art_prompt: A point rider surveying open country from a low rise, hand shading her eyes, horse and rider both in a working, unglamorous posture.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Background outfit crew, not a recruitable companion.

characters.name: Silas Rourke
characters.role: The rustler already in the Clear Fork room
characters.hook: Names and voices the rustler actor that already exists in scenes/room.tscn (currently silent). Per LORE.md: he may be carrying a mark that will not stay on a hide, and has his own strain. The room does not require a killing for flavor.
voice_lines: Man's got to eat. Don't make it personal.
You didn't see what I saw at the last water. I'm not going back to check.
Take the herd. Just don't ask why I stopped fighting for it.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, lean and sun-worn, dressed rough, visibly on his last luck.
characters.art_prompt: A rustler crouched low in tall grass at dusk, worn clothes, glancing over his shoulder at something off-screen rather than at the player -- he's spooked by more than the outfit.
continuity_notes: The rustler actor and its behavior are already implemented in scripts/room.gd; this record only proposes a name, voice and the 'own strain' framing from LORE.md. No banter file exists for him yet.

characters.name: Orin Teague
characters.role: The county's other blacksmith, resents Naomi Freeman's forge taking business
personality: genuinely skilled, which is what makes his resentment sting
characters.hook: A non-violent, personal antagonist directly tied to Naomi Freeman's madness stressor in characters.json ('a woman's forge work needs a man's name on it to count'). Best used for a reputation or business-rivalry beat rather than a fight.
voice_lines: Folks ride past my shop to hers now. I'd mind less if her work wasn't better.
Nobody asked my opinion on a woman running a forge. I'm giving it anyway.
I'll admit the wheel held. I won't admit I'm glad about it.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-forties, forge-built shoulders, a permanent scowl that's more habit than heat.
characters.art_prompt: A blacksmith at his own quieter forge, arms crossed, watching a customer's wagon head toward a rival's shop instead of his. Sullen rather than menacing.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Directly referenced by naomi_freeman's madness.personal_stressor in characters.json.

characters.name: Victor Ashgrove
characters.role: The theater manager who absconded with Marlowe Castellano's troupe's takings
personality: charming in exactly the way that should have been a warning sign
genuinely not violent, just a thief
always already gone by the time anyone catches up
characters.hook: The specific, low-stakes antagonist behind Marlowe Castellano's stranding -- a financial-crime figure rather than a physical threat, matching the Widow Stroud's non-violent antagonist pattern.
voice_lines: I didn't steal from them. I simply arrived at the bank before they did.
The show must go on. It's just going on somewhere I am and they aren't.
If Marlowe's found honest work, good. I did her a favor she'll never admit to.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, early forties, expensively but tastelessly dressed, always in motion toward an exit.
characters.art_prompt: A theater manager mid-stride away from a wagon, coat flaring, glancing back with an unbothered smile.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to marlowe_castellano.

characters.name: Fenwick Gray
characters.role: One of Roisin Dunmore's old associates, still working the illegitimate side of the trade
personality: genuinely fond of Roisin, which makes his pressure worse not better
characters.hook: The specific, recurring pressure behind Roisin Dunmore's 'almost took the job' backstory -- someone who keeps offering the old life back, sincerely, which is harder to refuse than a threat would be.
voice_lines: I'm not here to threaten you, Roisin. I'm here because the old crew misses you and the money's real.
Honest work pays slow. I remember when that used to bother you too.
I'll ask again next time our paths cross. I always do. You always say no. I keep asking anyway.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, early forties, well-dressed in a way that suggests money from somewhere unofficial, easy charming manner.
characters.art_prompt: A well-dressed man leaning in a doorway with an easy smile, the kind of charm that reads as a warning sign in retrospect.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to roisin_dunmore.

characters.name: Mortimer Vance
characters.role: The Widow Stroud's clerk, who actually delivers her collection notices in person
characters.hook: Softens the Widow Stroud's antagonist role with a human-scale employee who's uncomfortable with the work -- a possible source of leniency or advance warning if the outfit treats him decently.
voice_lines: I don't set the terms. I just deliver the paper. Please don't make me the villain of this conversation.
Mrs. Stroud would say I'm too soft for this work. I'd agree with her.
I could mention, unofficially, when a deadline's coming before it's official. I'm not supposed to.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-thirties, ill-fitting formal clothes, visibly uncomfortable with confrontation.
characters.art_prompt: A nervous clerk holding a folder of papers at someone's door, apologetic posture, clearly wishing he were elsewhere.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to the_widow_stroud.

characters.name: Inspector Wexler
characters.role: The territorial tax official investigating Adelheid Kraus's distilling operation
personality: not corrupt, genuinely just doing an unpopular job
characters.hook: The specific, non-violent bureaucratic threat behind Adelheid Kraus's encounter hook -- a legalistic antagonist who can be satisfied by actually correct paperwork, not defeated by force.
voice_lines: I don't make the tax code. I just have to enforce the part of it that reaches this county eventually.
If her operation's legitimate, a stamp and a fee solve this today. If it isn't, that's a longer conversation.
Everyone assumes I want to shut them down. Mostly I just want the paperwork to match reality.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late thirties, formal traveling clothes, a satchel of forms and stamps, patient bureaucratic manner.
characters.art_prompt: A tax inspector at a small camp table with official forms spread out, patient and unhurried, no menace intended in his posture.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to adelheid_kraus.

characters.name: Amos Ketch
characters.role: A third, more genuinely unpleasant independent trail-crew boss, contrasting Zilpah Hendricks's fairness
personality: outwardly friendly to outfits he wants something from
the actual bad-faith operator the Hargroves and Calloways are not
characters.hook: The county has two large, morally-mixed-but-not-villainous rival outfits (Calloway, Hargrove) and one small, fair independent (Zilpah). Ketch fills a real antagonist niche: an operator who actually treats people badly, giving the setting one clear bad actor without making either rival ranch flatly evil.
voice_lines: My crew works when I say and eats what's left over. That's the arrangement. They knew that going in.
Hendricks runs her outfit soft. Soft doesn't survive out here. We'll see whose crew is still riding in a year.
I'm friendly to whoever's useful to me today. Ask me again tomorrow if that's still you.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, fifty, superficially affable, harder eyes than his manner suggests.
characters.art_prompt: A trail-crew boss glad-handing a stranger with a broad smile that doesn't reach his eyes, crew visible in the background looking tired rather than loyal.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to zilpah_hendricks as a contrasting figure; the setting's clearest non-supernatural bad actor, distinct from the more sympathetic rival outfits.

characters.name: Silas Cobbett
characters.role: Editor of a rival Providence broadsheet that prints whatever sells
personality: not evil, just chose money over accuracy long ago
characters.hook: The specific person behind the exciting-false-story competition in Prisca Montaigne's encounter hook, giving her professional rivalry an actual face.
voice_lines: Truth sells fine. Excitement sells better. I stopped pretending otherwise years back.
Montaigne's paper is more honest than mine. It's also read by about a third as many people.
I'm not sorry. I am, occasionally, a little embarrassed. Different feeling entirely.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late forties, ink-stained but more polished than Prisca's shop, a hint of genuine talent under the cynicism.
characters.art_prompt: A rival newspaper editor at a busier, flashier print shop, reviewing lurid headline proofs with practiced indifference.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to prisca_montaigne.

characters.name: Dr. Barnabus Thistlewood
characters.role: The traveling salesman selling the harmful tonic Dinah Okonkwo exposes
personality: genuinely believes his own pitch more than he should
not malicious, just reckless and profit-driven
characters.hook: Names the specific antagonist behind Dinah Okonkwo's encounter hook -- a classic patent-medicine huckster, non-violent, defeated by evidence rather than force.
voice_lines: Dr. Thistlewood's Vital Restorative has cured more ailments than any licensed physician, by my own count.
I don't claim it's harmless. I claim it's effective. Those aren't always the same promise.
Miss Okonkwo's welcome to test it herself. I've found most chemists lack the courage of their convictions.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, early fifties, ostentatious traveling-salesman dress, practiced charming patter implied by posture.
characters.art_prompt: A patent-medicine salesman at a wagon stacked with colorful bottles, mid-pitch to a small skeptical crowd.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to dinah_okonkwo.

characters.name: Hosea Pruett
characters.role: A neighboring rancher who resents Briony Wexford's water usage for her dairy herd
personality: genuinely believes he's the wronged party
not violent, just petty and persistent
characters.hook: A small-scale, human-sized antagonist for Briony Wexford distinct from the county's larger rival-outfit or supernatural threats -- ordinary neighborly friction over water.

characters.name: The Drover Who Isn't
characters.role: Herd dead wearing the shape of an ordinary cowhand
personality: wants the count to match, for reasons that are not comforting
characters.hook: Per LORE.md's 'herd dead that want the count to match.' He rides drag on a strange outfit's herd, helpful and competent, until someone counts twice and gets two different numbers of riders.
voice_lines: Just passing the same trail you are. Funny how often that happens out here.
Count's off by one, isn't it. It's always off by one around me.
I don't eat. I don't sleep. I don't see why that should bother you if the work gets done.
characters.appearance_brief: An ordinary-looking cowhand at a glance; wrongness should only surface in specific, small details, not an obvious monster reveal.
characters.art_prompt: An unremarkable rider silhouetted against a herd at dusk, identical in gear and posture to any real drover -- the character design should intentionally NOT read as supernatural until a specific story beat reveals it.
continuity_notes: Not implemented.

characters.name: The Second Shadow
characters.role: A night hunter that is not a wolf
personality: avoids direct confrontation with fire or numbers
characters.hook: Per LORE.md's 'night hunters that are not wolves.' Its tell is that it casts a shadow the campfire shouldn't be able to produce, from a direction no source of light explains.
voice_lines: (does not speak; its presence is signaled by an extra shadow at the fire's edge, not dialogue)
characters.appearance_brief: Should not be shown directly in most encounters -- signaled through its shadow and the reaction of cattle and dogs rather than a clear character portrait.
characters.art_prompt: If ever depicted directly: a low, wolf-adjacent but visibly wrong silhouette at the treeline, cast shadow pointing the wrong direction relative to the campfire. Prefer showing only the wrong shadow over showing the creature itself.
continuity_notes: Not implemented. Deliberately kept mostly unshown, matching LORE.md's preference for implication over a monster-manual reveal.

characters.name: The Eight-Legged Doe
characters.role: An animal with too many joints, per LORE.md's list of wrong-country signs
characters.hook: A late-sign encounter for a place already gone strange (the Salt Flats). Its wrongness is in its gait and joint count, visible at a distance, not in any hostile act -- cattle refuse to cross where she's been seen.
voice_lines: (a wordless encounter; her wrongness reads through motion and cattle reaction, not speech)
characters.appearance_brief: A deer-like silhouette whose leg count and joint angles read as subtly, unmistakably wrong at a glance without needing gore or a monster redesign.
characters.art_prompt: A deer silhouette on the salt flats at heat-shimmer distance, extra leg joints suggested through unnatural stance rather than an over-designed creature. Keep it eerie through wrongness of motion/posture, not body horror.
continuity_notes: Not implemented.

characters.name: The Lantern Man
characters.role: A man who should have stayed buried and did not, per LORE.md's list
personality: polite in a way that is itself the warning sign
repeats the same small talk each encounter
does not seem to know he's dead
characters.hook: Distinct from the Ford Widow and the Drover Who Isn't -- this haunting's wrongness is social rather than physical: he offers ordinary trail courtesy (a shared fire, directions, a lantern to borrow) and the lantern he lends is always returned somewhere he never was. Late sign material per LORE.md, not an early one.
voice_lines: Evening. Cold one. You're welcome to share the fire, such as it is.
Take the lantern. I've got no more need of the light than I do the road.
I keep meaning to get back to town. Feels like I've been meaning to for some time now.
characters.appearance_brief: An ordinary-looking older traveler by firelight; his wrongness should surface only in small temporal/spatial inconsistencies, not appearance.
characters.art_prompt: A traveler at a small fire at night, offering a lantern toward the viewer, perfectly ordinary in appearance -- the unease should come from context and repetition across encounters, not from his design.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Tam
characters.role: A spirit-touched boy who runs messages between camps and outfits
characters.hook: A living child character used carefully: not a companion, not in danger for shock value, a message-carrier who treats the ordinary supernatural of this world exactly as ordinary as LORE.md says it is. His age is deliberately unspecified rather than stated, since he is not a romance-adjacent character and does not need one.
voice_lines: The lady at the crossing says to tell you she's still there. She always is, though.
Grown-ups ask if I'm scared. I don't know what I'd be scared of that isn't also just Tuesday.
I can carry a message further than a rumor. Rumors get things wrong on the way.
characters.appearance_brief: A child, practical patched clothes, unhurried in a way that unsettles adults more than it should.
characters.art_prompt: A boy sitting on a fence rail at dusk, relaxed posture, looking toward something off-screen that the viewer cannot see. Keep this depiction clearly childlike and non-sexualized; he is a courier character, not cast material.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Explicitly not romance-eligible; do not add him to characters.json under any circumstance.

characters.name: Hiram Cobb
characters.role: Willow Byrne's semi-retired former bounty-circuit partner
personality: still sharp despite the retirement talk
characters.hook: A friendly wanderer tied to Willow's backstory rather than a threat -- someone who could vouch for her, needle her about quitting, or bring one more old case to her door.
voice_lines: Byrne taught herself to quit. I never managed it. Ask me again in ten years.
She was the better tracker. I was better at knowing when to stop. We balanced out.
Tell her Cobb says hello, and that the offer to come back still stands, and that I already know she'll say no.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, mid-fifties, comfortable rather than hardened, gear well-used but not desperate.
characters.art_prompt: An older tracker resting against a fence post with a coffee, relaxed posture, watching the road rather than working it -- a man who has genuinely slowed down.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Percival Wren
characters.role: A traveling newspaper correspondent chasing tall-tale stories for an Eastern paper
personality: credulous in print, skeptical in person
will print the exciting version regardless of what actually happened
characters.hook: A comic-tinged wanderer who turns the outfit's real, mundane hardships into lurid tabloid copy -- a lens on how the Weird West gets flattened into myth even while it's happening, without the game itself needing to endorse that flattening.
voice_lines: A rustler and some spooked cattle. My editor will have it as a gunfight with the walking dead by Friday.
I don't need it to be true. I need it to sell papers in Boston.
Tell me the story again, and this time include a monster. My readers expect a monster.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late thirties, city clothes increasingly worn by trail conditions, notebook always out.
characters.art_prompt: An Eastern journalist taking notes with an ink pen, dust-covered good coat, comically overdressed for the trail compared to everyone around him.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Brother Amos
characters.role: An itinerant preacher circuit-riding between Providence, Griffin and smaller camps
personality: distinct from Reverend Pike -- has no fixed church at all
characters.hook: A wandering counterpart to Reverend Pike's settled congregation, useful for delivering a rumor or a moment of grace somewhere with no church building at all.
voice_lines: I preach wherever the fire is lit and someone's willing to listen. Most nights that's enough of a church.
Pike's got a roof going up. I've got a horse and a Bible. We compare notes when our trails cross.
I've buried more strangers than I've married couples out here. I try not to let that harden me.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, early fifties, simple worn coat, saddlebags that carry more sermons than possessions.
characters.art_prompt: An itinerant preacher on horseback at a crossroads, hat in hand, a small worn Bible visible in a saddlebag.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/.

characters.name: Captain Ines Fournier
characters.role: Josephine Merriweather's former riverboat captain, now retired to a shore job
personality: genuinely fond of her old crew
misses the river as much as Josephine does
characters.hook: Gives Josephine Merriweather's backstory a specific former colleague/mentor, and a possible route back to river work if that thread is ever picked up.
voice_lines: Merriweather kept my boilers honest for six years. Land's lucky to have her, if land deserves it.
I retired because my knees quit before my nerve did. She's got years left in her, out there or in here.
Tell her the old girl's still afloat, if she ever wants to see a proper boiler again.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult woman, fifty, weathered river-trade coat, the particular squint of someone who spent decades watching water.
characters.art_prompt: A retired riverboat captain on a porch far from any river, looking distinctly out of place and slightly wistful about it.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to josephine_merriweather.

characters.name: Old Ansel Vogt
characters.role: The retired falconer who trained Artemisia Falk
personality: genuinely proud of his student surpassing him
half-retired, still keeps one old hawk
characters.hook: Gives Artemisia Falk a mentor and continuity anchor, and a source of falconry lore/rumors distinct from the county's other trades.
voice_lines: I taught her to listen to the birds instead of talking at them. She listens better than I ever did.
My hands aren't steady enough for the gauntlet anymore. Hers are.
A hawk doesn't lie about trust. Neither does a good student, eventually.
characters.appearance_brief: Adult man, late sixties, weathered, one old hooded hawk still on a perch beside him.
characters.art_prompt: An old falconer on a porch with a single aged hawk, watching a younger falconer's silhouette in the distance with quiet pride.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to artemisia_falk.

characters.name: Little Pim
characters.role: Temperance Boucher's cooperage apprentice, a quiet orphan she took in
personality: clearly attached to Temperance beyond just the trade
characters.hook: Gives Temperance Boucher an unexpected soft edge -- she's quietly raising an apprentice who isn't just staff to her, without making it a romance thread. Treated with the same careful non-romantic precedent as Tam and Tobias Ochoa.
voice_lines: Miss Boucher says a barrel that leaks is worse than no barrel at all. I believe everything she tells me.
She doesn't talk about where I came from. I don't ask. Seems like a fair trade.
I want a shop of my own someday. She says I'll have earned it by the time I'm ready.
characters.appearance_brief: A young apprentice covered in wood shavings, watching a cooper work with clear devotion and attention.
characters.art_prompt: A child apprentice handing tools to a cooper at a workbench, small and careful movements, clearly trusted with real responsibility. Keep clearly childlike and non-sexualized, a background family-adjacent character, not cast material -- same treatment as little_tam and tobias_ochoa.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to temperance_boucher. Explicitly not romance-eligible; do not add to characters.json under any circumstance.

characters.name: Old Meredith Snow
characters.role: An elderly weather-reader who warned Rosamund Achterberg about the coming frost
personality: genuinely accurate about weather far more often than chance would explain
treated as an ordinary local expert, not a mystic
characters.hook: A grounded, non-supernatural weather-prediction source who gives Rosamund Achterberg's frost crisis its early warning, matching LORE.md's preference for ordinary explanations where one suffices.
voice_lines: My knees ache different for snow than for frost. Tonight it's frost, and it's coming hard.
Forty years reading this sky. I don't need a spirit to tell me what my own joints already know.
Achterberg listens when I talk. Most folks wait until the ice is already on the ground.
characters.appearance_brief: An elderly woman, weathered and slightly stooped, gazing at the sky with practiced attention rather than mystical performance.
characters.art_prompt: An old woman on a porch studying cloud formations, cane in hand, practical and grounded rather than eerie.
continuity_notes: Not implemented in scripts/. Ties to rosamund_achterberg. Deliberately given a mundane explanation (experience, not supernatural gift) per LORE.md's instruction to keep the ordinary world ordinary.
